scene_prompt: Modern elementary classroom model-building activity. Stubborn child tries to force a square wooden peg into a clearly circular hole in a shape board, frowning and refusing to listen. Teacher kneels kindly and points out matching square hole immediately nearby; classmate demonstrates the same square peg fitting easily into a second square hole on identical board. Main child turns face away from their sensible explanation, shoulders rigid, continues pressing square peg against round opening. Board intact, no injuries, no power tools. Key is repeated obvious explanation ignored through stubborn refusal to understand, not simple learning difficulty. Gentle depiction without mocking intellectual disability, no stigmatizing features. Natural hands five fingers, correct wrists, peg-square versus circular aperture visibly incompatible, grounded table and coherent perspective. 3:2 landscape, graphite watercolor colored pencil ivory paper, no readable text labels letters numbers brands or watermarks.
alt: 老師和同學示範方形木塊應放進方孔，孩子卻轉頭不聽，仍固執地把方塊往圓孔裡塞。
